name: Medibank OSHC Team
subject: ⚠ YOUR COVER HAS EXPIRED!!!
body: Your Overseas Student Health Cover has EXPIRED. Renew within 2 hours or your visa may be cancelled.

flags.greeting: Generic greeting. Medibank knows your name
flags.body: Threats and a 2-hour deadline are pressure tactics
flags.link: The real domain is medibank-oshc-renew.xyz, not medibank.com.au

tip: Real insurers never threaten visa cancellation by email.

name: ATO Refund Centre
subject: Tax Refund Available
body: A tax refund of $1,284 is ready. Claim within 24 hours or it will expire.

flags.sender: The ATO only uses ato.gov.au, never '.net'
flags.body: Unexpected money plus a 24-hour deadline is a classic lure

tip: Unexpected refunds are bait. Check myGov directly.

name: Swinburne Student Services
subject: Semester Timetable
body: Your Semester 2 timetable is now available on the student portal.
tip: Neutral emails with an official domain are usually fine.
why: Official .edu.au domain, personal greeting, no threats, no requests for credentials.

name: PayPal Security
subject: Urgent Login Alert
body: Suspicious activity detected. Verify now to avoid suspension.
tip: Hyphenated brand names are a warning sign.

name: Spotify
subject: New Playlist For You
body: We picked some songs based on your recent listening.
tip: Marketing emails can be real. Check domain and demands.
why: Official spotify.com domain, harmless content, no credential request.

name: Student Rewards
subject: 🎉 You've WON a $1,000 gift card!
body: You were randomly selected! Enter your card details to receive your prize today.

flags.sender: A random '.top' domain is not a real retailer
flags.body: You can't win a contest you never entered, and prizes never need card details
flags.link: Prize site collects your card details

tip: If it sounds too good to be true, it is.

name: Medibank Claims
subject: Your OSHC refund of $246.80 is pending
body: Your recent claim was overpaid. Confirm your bank details to receive your refund.

flags.body: Real refunds go to details already on file, not via email links
flags.link: Subdomain trick: the real domain is secure-refund.net

tip: Read a domain right to left from the first single '/'.

name: Medibank
subject: Your OSHC claim has been processed
body: Your claim from 12 March has been processed. View the details in your Medibank account or app.
tip: Real emails tell you what happened without demanding data.
why: Official medibank.com.au domain, personal greeting, no urgency, no data requests.

name: Dept of Home Affairs
subject: Student visa under review – action required
body: Your student visa is under review. Upload a photo of your passport and bank statement within 24 hours.

flags.greeting: Generic greeting for a personal visa matter
flags.body: Passport and bank documents plus a 24-hour deadline
flags.link: homeaffairs-gov.com is a lookalike, not homeaffairs.gov.au

tip: Government agencies use .gov.au and don't ask for documents via email links.

name: Daniel Kim
subject: Re: Room in Carlton – holding deposit
body: Great to meet you! To hold the room, transfer a $600 deposit today. I have other applicants.

flags.sender: A free webmail address for a 'property manager'
flags.body: Pressure to pay before an inspection or lease is a rental scam sign
flags.link: Payment page on an unrelated '.top' domain

tip: Never pay a deposit before inspecting and seeing a lease.

name: Monash Student Admin
subject: Your assignment 2 result is available
body: Your result has been released. Sign in to the student portal to see your grade and feedback.
tip: A subdomain of the real domain (student.monash.edu) is fine.
why: Sender and link both belong to monash.edu; the tone is calm and informational.

name: PTV
subject: Your myki top-up receipt
body: Thanks for topping up $20. No action is needed.
tip: 'No action needed' is a good sign.
why: Victorian government domain, receipt only, nothing to click or enter.

name: Medibank OSHC
subject: Priya, your OSHC cover ends 31 December
body: To keep your cover active, please confirm your details by 31 Dec. It only takes a minute.

flags.link: The '@' trick: everything before '@' is ignored. You land on verify-oshc-members.net

tip: Spear-phishing uses your name. Always check the real domain.

name: Swinburne IT Helpdesk
subject: Password expires in 3 days
body: Your Swinburne password expires soon. Sign in with single sign-on to keep access to email and Canvas.

flags.link: Subdomain trick: the real domain is login-portal.net

tip: Go to the portal yourself instead of clicking.

name: Medibank
subject: Your OSHC card is ready
body: Your digital card is ready in the Medibank app. Your cover renews on 31 December. No action is needed unless your details changed.
tip: A date isn't a threat. Look for pressure and requests.
why: Official domain, mentions a date but with no pressure, no request for credentials.

name: Dr. M. Chen
subject: Grade appeal – please review
body: I've reviewed your appeal. The outcome is in a shared document. Sign in with your uni account to open it.

flags.body: Asks you to sign in with uni credentials to read a document
flags.link: Looks like Google Drive but the real domain is shared-docs.cc

tip: Even a plausible lecturer can be spoofed. Verify via the portal.

name: Swinburne Accommodation
subject: Lease renewal reminder
body: Your lease ends on 28 Feb. Renewal forms will be on the student portal when you're ready.
tip: A reminder with no deadline pressure is normal.
why: Official domain and a calm reminder pointing to a portal you already use.

name: Medibank Claims
subject: Claim rejected – appeal within 12 hours
body: Your claim #48213 was rejected due to a missing document. Appeal within 12 hours or the claim will lapse.

flags.body: A 12-hour deadline to push you into acting

tip: Zoom in on letters: 'rn' looks like 'm'.
